title: Voyager 1 Launch
description: Voyager 1 was launched aboard a Titan IIIE-Centaur rocket from Launch Complex 41 at Cape Canaveral, Florida, on a faster trajectory to Jupiter and Saturn.

title: First Earth-Moon Crescent Portrait
description: Voyager 1 captured the first photograph in history showing both the entire Earth and Moon in a single frame, taken from a distance of 11.66 million kilometers.

title: Jupiter Closest Approach
description: Closest approach to Jupiter at 277,000 km. Discovered active volcanoes on moon Io, thin rings around Jupiter, and two new moons (Thebe and Metis).

title: Saturn & Titan Closest Approach
description: Passed 6,490 km from smog-shrouded moon Titan and 124,000 km from Saturn. Gravity assist hurled Voyager 1 northward out of the ecliptic plane at 35 degrees.

title: The "Pale Blue Dot" Family Portrait
description: Looking back toward Earth from 6.06 billion km (40.5 AU), Voyager 1 took the famous "Pale Blue Dot" photo and Solar System Family Portrait before cameras were turned off forever to save power.

title: Most Distant Human-Made Object
description: Voyager 1 officially surpassed Pioneer 10 at 69.4 AU from the Sun to become the most distant spacecraft built by humankind.

title: Termination Shock Crossing
description: Crossed the termination shock at 94 AU, where the supersonic solar wind abruptly slows to subsonic speeds upon interaction with interstellar magnetic fields.

title: Crossing into Interstellar Space
description: Crossed the heliopause at 121.6 AU, registering a complete disappearance of solar wind particles and a dramatic surge in galactic cosmic rays. The first human probe in interstellar space.

title: Current Interstellar Journey
description: Voyager 1 operates at over 166 AU from the Sun, continuing to transmit magnetic field and plasma wave measurements to Earth via NASA Deep Space Network.

title: Voyager 2 Launch
description: Voyager 2 launched 16 days before Voyager 1 on a longer, more fuel-conserving trajectory designed to enable visits to Uranus and Neptune if the spacecraft survived.

title: Jupiter Closest Approach
description: Flew past Jupiter at 570,000 km, capturing intricate time-lapse footage of atmospheric eddies, Jupiter's rings, and surface fractures across Europa.

title: Saturn Closest Approach
description: Closest approach to Saturn at 101,000 km. Evaluated ring structure variations via stellar occultations and used Saturnian gravity to slingshot towards Uranus.

title: Uranus Historic Encounter
description: The ONLY spacecraft in human history to visit Uranus. Made closest approach at 81,500 km, discovered 10 new moons, 2 rings, and mapped extreme 59-degree tilted magnetosphere.

title: Neptune Historic Encounter
description: The ONLY spacecraft in human history to visit Neptune. Flew just 4,950 km above Neptune's north pole, photographed Great Dark Spot, and discovered active nitrogen geysers on moon Triton.

title: Termination Shock Crossing
description: Crossed the termination shock at 84 AU into the southern heliosheath, proving that the heliosphere is asymmetrical and squashed in the southern quadrant.

title: Crossing into Interstellar Space
description: Entered interstellar space at 119 AU. Unlike Voyager 1 whose plasma instrument failed in 1980, Voyager 2's functioning PLS instrument provided humanity's first direct measurements of interstellar plasma density.

title: Current Interstellar Journey
description: Voyager 2 travels through interstellar space at ~138 AU from the Sun, continuing long-term heliosphere boundary and galactic cosmic ray research.
